vid.img_strength.tt:
Quanto il video resta fedele al fotogramma di partenza.
0.45-0.60 = movimento naturale (consigliato, 'soft reference').
0.80+ = aderenza stretta ma movimento più rigido.
vid.i2v_method.tt:
Come l'immagine di partenza condiziona il video:
• AddGuide multi-keyframe: guida ad attenzione, supporta più keyframe (catena attuale).
• Inplace soft: scrive l'immagine nel 1° frame del latent + noise_mask (1-forza). Avvio 'fisico' dall'immagine con movimento naturale — replica il workflow di riferimento. La «Forza immagine» qui sopra controlla quanto il 1° frame resta fedele.
vid.downscale: Downscale 50% (genera a metà risoluzione — più veloce, meno dettaglio)
vid.downscale.tt:
OFF (default) = generazione NATIVA a piena risoluzione → massimo dettaglio.
ON = genera a metà e poi ingrandisce in bicubico (più veloce, più molle, ma nasconde il reticolo del decoder VAE).
vid.upscale: Upscale ×2 (super-risoluzione spaziale latente — più nitido, più lento)
vid.refine: Refine HR (passata di dettaglio tiled — più definizione, più lento)
vid.note_res: W/H arrotondati a multipli di 32. Con 'Auto', NSFW seleziona 10EROS; SFW il distilled 1.1.
vid.fr_auto: Restaura i volti al termine della generazione (CodeFormer / GFPGAN)
vid.fr_auto.tt: Dopo aver generato il video, applica automaticamente un restauro volti per-fotogramma che corregge l'aspetto «plastico» e la deriva d'identità di LTX, PRESERVANDO l'identità (non ri-genera col diffusion).
vid.fr_auto_fidelity.tt: 1.0 preserva di più l'originale; 0.0 ricostruisce di più (più nitido, può scostarsi). ~0.7 consigliato.
vid.fr_note: Richiede il custom node facerestore_cf (installabile da «Migliora qualità → Video»). I modelli (~350MB) si scaricano al primo uso.

Utile per prompt brevi; con prompt già dettagliati lascialo OFF. In NSFW inietta automaticamente la direttiva di sblocco.
adv.samp.sampler.tt:
Sampler VERIFICATI compatibili con LTX-2.3:
• euler_ancestral_cfg_pp — DEFAULT, qualità migliore (reference AuthorStorm)
• euler_cfg_pp / euler — deterministici, robusti
• dpmpp_2m — alternativa valida
⚠ I sampler RES (res_2s, res_multistep…) sono stati RIMOSSI: in teoria ottimi per il flow, ma in pratica producono RUMORE verde su LTX-2.3 (verificato A/B).
adv.samp.scheduler.tt:
Ora EFFETTIVO anche sul video:
• LTXVScheduler (shift) — default: usa l'LTXVScheduler con gli SHIFT qui sotto (consigliato, flow-aware, shape-aware)
• linear_quadratic — schedule nativo LTX
• bong_tangent / kl_optimal / beta57 — alta qualità (flow-aware)
• karras — dettaglio (diffusione) · beta — distilled · exponential — morbido
Scegliendo uno scheduler classico, gli Shift LTX vengono ignorati.
adv.samp.base_shift.tt: Shift BASE di LTXVScheduler (default 0.95). Più ALTO = più step su struttura e MOVIMENTO (coerenza temporale, meno flicker); più BASSO = più dettaglio fine ma rischio di incoerenza tra frame. È la leva qualità #1 del video LTX.
adv.samp.max_shift.tt: Shift MAX di LTXVScheduler (default 2.05). Limite superiore dello shift dipendente dalla risoluzione/lunghezza. Alzalo per clip più lunghe/grandi se il movimento è incerto.
adv.samp.encoder.tt:
Encoder testo del VIDEO LTX — incide soprattutto sull'ADERENZA al prompt (composizione, soggetto, azione), meno sulla texture:
• Gemma 3 12B full — massima fedeltà semantica, ma 'ammorbidisce' i contenuti espliciti
• Gemma 3 12B abliterated — versione decensurata: molto migliore su prompt NSFW spinti
Stesso 12B → nessuna perdita di velocità tra i due. '⛔ assente' = file non ancora presente.

adv.lv.auto: Genera automaticamente i video più lunghi della soglia (a spezzoni)
adv.lv.auto.tt: Se attivo, quando la durata richiesta nel tab Video supera la soglia qui sotto, il video viene prodotto in una passata base + estensioni automatiche a spezzoni (lunghezza illimitata, VRAM costante).
adv.lv.threshold.tt: Durata massima della singola passata LTX. Oltre questa, scatta l'estensione automatica. LTX-2.3 arriva a ~20s nativi in passata singola → tienila a 20.
adv.lv.seg.tt: Lunghezza di ogni spezzone I2V concatenato. Più lungo = meno giunzioni = meno transizioni. Consigliato 10s.
adv.lv.overlap.tt: Fotogrammi DROPPATI all'inizio di ogni spezzone (nascondono la transizione I2V dal frame statico). 24 = 1s @24fps. Più alti = transizioni più pulite ma più contenuto scartato.
adv.lv.context.tt: Fotogrammi della coda usati come contesto per lo spezzone successivo.
adv.lv.ctx_strength.tt: Quanto il contesto vincola lo spezzone: 1.0=molto ancorato (meno deriva, meno movimento), 0.0=libero (più movimento, più deriva).

ext.duration.tt: Durata totale da aggiungere. Nessun limite: viene generata a spezzoni concatenati (memory-bounded → lunghezza illimitata).
ext.seg.tt:
Lunghezza di ogni spezzone QUANDO si supera la soglia di 20s.
Regola: ≤20s → UNA passata unica (nessuna giunzione → niente segmento nero); >20s → spezzoni da questo valore (default 18s) con sovrapposizione.
ext.overlap.tt: Fotogrammi di sovrapposizione tra spezzoni (continuità di moto).
ext.context.tt: Fotogrammi della coda usati come contesto per lo spezzone successivo (continuità). Più alto = più ancorato al passato.
ext.note.lbl: Lunghezza illimitata. Fino a 20s si genera in una passata unica (nessuna giunzione → niente segmento nero). Oltre i 20s si divide in spezzoni da ~18s con sovrapposizione, ognuno condizionato sulla coda del precedente (decodifica per spezzone → VRAM costante). Tag SSML supportati nel prompt.

cn.intro.lbl: ControlNet copia il movimento/forma da un video di riferimento al video generato. Il contenuto rimane definito dal prompt nel tab Video; il movimento è dettato dal video qui caricato. Tutti e tre i tipi sono completamente implementati nel workflow.
cn.enable: ✅ Abilita ControlNet (copia il movimento dal video qui sotto)
cn.video.hint.lbl: Il video deve avere movimento chiaramente leggibile (es. per Pose: il soggetto deve essere ben visibile). Risoluzione e durata: indifferenti — il workflow ricampiona alla risoluzione del tab Video e tronca alla durata configurata.
cn.usage.lbl:
1. Configura: abilita la checkbox sopra, scegli il tipo, carica il video di riferimento.
2. Prompt: nel tab Video scrivi il prompt che descrive il contenuto del video che vuoi generare (soggetto, ambiente, stile). Il prompt è obbligatorio — descrive la scena.
3. Lancia: dal pannello principale, bottone «🎬 Genera» (in basso a sinistra, lo stesso del flusso normale).

Esempio: video reference = persona che balla → prompt = «una ballerina con abito rosso danza in una sala elegante, illuminazione soffusa» → il modello produce una ballerina con quel movimento.

L'integrazione Kontext armonizza già senza (riferimento + prompt). Lasciala spenta.

f1.seg.threshold.tt:
Soglia di selezione (agisce su ENTRAMBE le modalità):
• Da testo (GroundingDINO): confidenza minima del detector.
• Col puntatore (SAM): soglia della maschera.
Valori ALTI (0.50-0.70) = selezione più stretta/precisa; BASSI (0.20-0.35) = più ampia (prende tutto l'oggetto). Se col click prende solo una macchia, ABBASSALA.
f1.seg.hint: Da testo (🎯 Seleziona): GroundingDINO trova l'oggetto descritto; con +SAM-HQ ne rifinisce il bordo. Col puntatore (click/riquadro sul canvas): SAM vanilla raffina la regione disegnata. La maschera risultante è modificabile a mano con pennello/gomma.

f1.restore.tt:

• Colorazione B&W → colore (FLUX.2)
• Restauro + Colorazione combinati

Da dove viene la voce (albero di decisione del tab Audio):
1. File audio caricato nel tab Audio (modalità «Audio fornito da me») → si usa quel file (lip-sync su di esso).
2. Altrimenti, se è selezionata una voce nel TTS e c'è del testo nel campo TTS → si sintetizza il testo con quella voce (clonata o no) e si fa il lip-sync.
3. Altrimenti → si usa il dialogo scritto nel prompt principale e la voce la genera LTX (es. «…she says: "…", perfect lip-sync»).

settings.stego.tt: Embeds an invisible, imperceptible signature into every generated photo/video, allowing you to verify (with the ATF Detector tool) that the content was created with this software. It does not visibly alter the image. Enabled by default.
settings.stego_text.tt: Custom text (max 5 characters, e.g. your own code/handle) embedded invisibly and readable by the Detector. Empty = valid signature without text. The 5-character limit is to resist screenshots/compression; for longer text use the file metadata.
settings.native_hint: Chooses how models are loaded. ComfyUI-native uses dynamic VRAM management (no OOM); Diffusers/LTX-2 use the native pipelines.

cn.strength_hint: 1.0 = strictly follows the reference; lower values = more creative freedom.
music.adv.steps.tt: Denoising steps. More steps = more detail and cleaner audio (but slower). 60 is a good compromise; below ~30 grey noise may appear.
music.gs_lyric.tt: Adherence to the LYRICS (ACE-Step, Double Condition Guidance). Together with 'Style adherence' it enables double guidance: BOTH must be >1.0 to take effect. 3-5 = more faithful lyrics. 0 = disables double guidance (falls back to CFG only).
music.meta.title: 🎼  Musical metadata (BPM, key, time signature, language)

music.meta.key.tt: Key/scale (e.g. C major, A minor). Minor keys sound darker/more melancholic, major keys brighter. (auto) = chosen by the model.
music.meta.timesig.tt: Time signature/meter. 4/4 for most pop/rock/hip-hop/electronic, 3/4 for waltz, 6/8 for ballads. (auto) = chosen by the model.
music.meta.lang.tt: Singing language. (auto) = detected automatically from the lyrics. Set it if detection is wrong or if the lyrics mix multiple languages.
music.sections.tt: Inserts [{s}] at the cursor position in the lyrics.

post.last.tt: Use the last generated track as source.

post.trim.tt: Removes silence at start and end (and long internal gaps).
post.fmt.tt: Output format. (unchanged) = keeps the source one.
music.task.extract.tt: Isolates a track (vocals/drums/bass…) from a mix. Requires the ACE-Step 1.5 foundation.
music.task.lego.tt: Overlays a single instrumental track onto existing audio. Requires ACE-Step 1.5.
music.task.complete.tt: Fills in the missing instruments of a partial track. Requires ACE-Step 1.5.
music.task.cover.tt: Re-sings a song in a new style. Requires ACE-Step 1.5.
music.task.remix.tt: Regenerates structure/style from a guide audio. Requires ACE-Step 1.5.
music.task.sel.tt: Type of ACE-Step operation. The 🔒 entries require the 1.5 foundation.
music.spectro.tt: Opens the spectrogram of the last track and lets you compare it with another (spectral centroid).
music.region.set: Region [{a:.1f}–{b:.1f}s] set to Repaint (regenerates only that part).
music.est.tt: Estimates VRAM load based on duration × batch × steps × quantization (green ok, yellow near the limit, red offload/OOM risk). The time estimate is indicative and depends on the GPU.
music.preset.tt: Saved style configurations. Select to load.
music.preset.save.tt: Saves the current parameters as a new preset.
music.preset.name: Preset name:

music.preset.nosc: No parameters found for this track.
music.tagpicker.btn.tt: Pick style tags from the palette
music.adherence.tt: Adherence to the style tags (ACE-Step, Double Condition Guidance). Only active if >1.0; 3-5 = the style tags weigh more. 0/≤1 = off (combined CFG only).
music.reset.tt: Resets all parameters to the optimal values of the selected model.
music.lastvideo.tt: Use the last video generated in the app
music.cfg.hm.tt: CFG = adherence to tags/lyrics (HeartMuLa's only lever). Higher = more faithful; beyond ~4-5 risks artifacts/repetitions. For best adherence use the RL checkpoint.
music.cfg.ace.tt: ACE-Step CFG (apg). ~15 is the sweet spot. For adherence to the TAGS also use 'Style adherence'.
music.reset.done: Parameters reset to the defaults of {e}
music.train.confirm.m: I'll train the LoRA '{name}' on {n} files for {s} steps. This may take a long time. Continue?
music.adv.erg.tt: ERG keeps adherence while increasing diversity/quality. Recommended ON. Turn off for more deterministic but less varied results.
music.adv.title: ⚙️  Advanced (ACE-Step)
music.adv.hm_note: ⓘ These controls are only available with the ACE-Step engine. Select ACE-Step to use them.
music.adv.scheduler.tt:
Sampler.
• pingpong (SDE): best coherence and style/lyrics alignment (recommended for adherence)
• euler: fast and standard
• heun: more precise but slower
music.adv.cfgtype.tt:
Guidance algorithm.
• apg: recommended (stable, great prompt adherence)
• cfg: classic Classifier-Free Guidance
• cfg_star: a more recent variant
music.adv.omega.tt: Controls the scheduler variance (default 10). Higher values = greater track consistency.
music.adv.ginterval.tt: Fraction of steps in which guidance is active (0.5 = first half). Lower = guidance only at the start.
music.adv.gdecay.tt: Decay of guidance toward the minimum during sampling (0 = constant). >0 = more natural results toward the end.
music.adv.ming.tt: Floor of the guidance when it decays (default 3.0).
music.adv.format.tt:
Output format.
• wav / flac: lossless
• mp3 / ogg: compressed (smaller files)
music.adv.seed.tt: Generation seed. Empty = random every time. Fixing it (e.g. 42) makes the result REPRODUCIBLE. Multiple comma-separated seeds for batch.
music.adv.batch.tt: How many songs to generate in one go (multiple variants of the same prompt).
music.adv.quantized.tt: Loads the quantized model: uses LESS VRAM while staying on GPU (faster than 'Low VRAM', which offloads weights to CPU).
music.adv.overlap.tt: Overlapped decoding: less memory and faster in the final audio decoding stage.
music.adv.compile.tt: Compiles the model: faster after the first run (the first compilation takes extra time).
music.adv.lora.tt: Applies a trained LoRA (e.g. the one produced by the trainer below) to the generation.
music.task.retake.tt: Regenerates the same track with variations. 'Variance' controls how much it changes.
music.task.repaint.tt: Regenerates ONLY a time range of the source audio, preserving the rest.
music.task.edit.tt: Changes the style tags or lyrics of an existing track while PRESERVING melody and voice.
music.task.extend.tt: Adds music before/after the source audio.
music.task.a2a.tt: Generates guided by a REFERENCE audio (style-transfer). 'Strength' adjusts how much to follow it.
music.task.title: 🎛️  Operation (ACE-Step)
music.task.src.tt: Audio file to operate on (repaint/edit/extend) or reference (audio2audio).
music.task.var.tt: 0 = almost identical to the original · 1 = very different.
music.task.rstart.tt: Start (seconds) of the section to regenerate/extend.
music.task.rend.tt: End (seconds) of the section to regenerate/extend.
music.task.eprompt.tt: New style tags for the edit (empty = use the main tags).
music.task.elyrics.tt: New lyrics for the edit (empty = use the main lyrics). Edit small bits at a time.
music.task.str.tt: How much to follow the reference audio (0=little, 1=a lot).

vedit.dilate.tt: How much to GROW the tracked mask (px): more room for the new object, less tight borders.
cn.attn.tt: conditioning_attention_strength: 1.0 = attention strictly bound to the guide video; lower values (0.5-0.8) allow more creative freedom while preserving motion.
f1.inpaint.feather.tt: Feather of the edge between regenerated area and original (px): Auto = proportional to the photo; higher = softer transition but wider edit ring.

emb.cache.title: Prompt embedding cache
emb.cache.tt: Every video generation recomputes the prompt encoding by re-reading 24 GB of text encoder from disk (~13 seconds). With the cache the same prompt is reused: a long video in 6 segments computes it once instead of six times. The result is identical, it is the same tensor. Entries hold the prompt text in clear and live in data/emb_cache.

vid.h3.turbo.tt: lightx2v distillation LoRA: from ~49 down to 4 or 8 steps (10× faster). With references (Ref2VA) only the 4-step preview exists.

vid.h3.dur: Actual length: {s:.2f} s ({n} frames at 24 fps)
vid.h3.no_cfg: MiniMax H3 has distilled guidance: no negative prompt and no CFG.
h3.dlg.speaker: Speaker
h3.dlg.add.tt: Adds a spoken line: H3 generates the voice together with the video, with synced lips. Pick the language of each line.
avatar.voice.language.tt: Language of the TEXT this person reads. It differs from the voice's language: Edge and Kokoro voices speak one language only (text in another language comes out with their accent), cloned voices and Edge "Multilingual" voices speak every language with the sample's timbre. For a sentence in another language inside a line use [lang:en]…[/lang].
avatar.voice.accent.tt: Tick it if you deliberately want a voice from another language on this text (e.g. English with an Italian accent): no language-mismatch warning.
f1.gen.qwen21.turbo_int8: Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo INT8 (8 steps, any GPU)
f1.gen.qwen21.turbo_fixed: The Turbo checkpoint uses its own schedule: 8 steps, CFG 1.
f1.gen.qwen21.i2i.tt: Redraws an existing photo following the prompt: keeps composition and colors, changes style and details. Unlike references, which the model reinterprets freely.
f1.gen.qwen21.strength.tt: How much to redraw: 0.30 = light touch-up, 0.60 = new style on the same scene, 1.00 = from scratch.
f1.color.model.tt: Qwen-Image 2.1 model used for the color change.
mw.qwen21_no_init: img2img: load a photo into the canvas or pick one in the «Starting image» field.
mw.qwen21_no_dit: Choose the Qwen-Image 2.1 model in the panel menu.
mw.qwen21_no_prompt: Write WHAT to change in the instruction.
weights.use.uncensored: Uncensored (18+): nudity and explicit content without filters; visible only in NSFW mode.
f1.gen.qwen21.te.tt: Encoder that reads prompt and references. «Paired» = the one intended for the chosen model; NVFP4 works with any model on RTX 50xx and saves memory.
f1.gen.qwen21.i2i.hint: 💡 img2img keeps composition, colors and the photographic look: 0.30-0.60 touches up, 0.85-1.00 redraws more. To change the STYLE while keeping the subject (e.g. «the person in image 1 as a Japanese print») use References: that is what Qwen-Image 2.1 is trained for.
f1.gen.qwen21.i2i.to_ref: Use the photo as a reference
f1.gen.qwen21.i2i.to_ref.tt: Moves the starting image to References (image 1) and turns img2img off: then describe in the prompt how to transform it.
f1.gen.qwen21.pe.tt: With «✨ Enhance prompt» on, Qwen-Image 2.1 uses its official enhancers: they rewrite the request (in any language) into a detailed English prompt; when editing they also look at the images. «Thorough» reasons before writing: more accurate, much slower.
f1.gen.qwen21.cn.tt: The image follows the composition of a photo (edges, depth, lines) while prompt and style decide the rest. Works with text-to-image and img2img, not together with References.
f1.gen.qwen21.cn.kind.tt: How to extract the structure from the guide photo. «Already a map» uses the image as is: for a pose skeleton, a sketch or a map prepared elsewhere.
f1.gen.qwen21.cn.scale.tt: How closely to follow the structure: 1.00 = faithful (official value), lower = more freedom for the prompt.
mw.qwen21_no_control: ControlNet: load a photo into the canvas or pick one in the «Guide photo» field.
mw.qwen21_control_refs: ControlNet can't be combined with References: turn one of them off.
weights.use.prompt_enhancer: Prompt enhancer: an LLM rewrites your request into a detailed prompt before generating.
fs.sb.qwen21_dit.tt: Qwen-Image 2.1 model for keyframes and cast portraits.
f1.gen.krea2.te.tt: Encoder that reads the prompt. “Uncensored” describes explicit content without softening it; works with Turbo, Raw and Krea Noct.
vid.ltx_te.tt: Encoder that reads the prompt for LTX 2.5. “Uncensored” describes explicit content without softening it; works with every 2.5 transformer.
weights.civitai.hint: civitai.com → Account settings → API Keys (stays on this PC only)
weights.civitai.tt: Needed for models sourced from Civitai: without a key Civitai redirects to the login page and the download fails.
weights.use.veda_sparse: Veda sparse attention: a small predictor computes only the attention blocks that matter — faster H3 video, same weights.
vid.h3.veda.tt: Computes only the attention blocks a trained predictor marks as useful: about 1.4–2.2× faster denoising. Works with references (Ref2VA) and Turbo 8 steps; the model weights do not change. If anything does not fit, the video falls back to full attention on its own.
vid.h3.turbo.v4: Turbo v4 8 steps (larryvrh, also with references)
vid.h3.vae.tt: Pruned version of the H3 video VAE (lightx2v): same latents, so the model does not change. The Lite decoder turns latents into frames about 3 times faster with half the video memory; the Lite encoder also speeds up encoding of the first/last image and references. It may lose some fine detail: compare it with the original.
f1.inpaint.klein_te.tt: Text encoder of FLUX.2 Klein 9B. The uncensored version is the same Qwen3-8B with the tendency to refuse removed: it follows explicit prompts instead of softening them. It applies to all jobs made with Klein 9B (inpaint, Integrate, Compose, Color); it is not used with Klein 4B.
vid.h3.turbo.dmad: Turbo DMAD + v4, 8 steps (better audio, experimental)
v2v.wanlora_note: Talk and Sing run on Wan 2.1 + MultiTalk: pick the Wan LoRAs here (style, detail, concepts). They are added on top of the built-in distillation LoRA; the LTX panel LoRAs do not apply to Wan.
vedit.note_refocus: Fixes ONLY lens blur (out of focus). For motion blur use “Reduce motion blur”.
vedit.note_uncompress: Removes compression artifacts (blocking, banding, mosquito noise, ringing). The source video is the guide: no other fields.
vedit.note_deinterlace: Removes interlacing combing and frame blending. Preview: little tested.
vedit.note_motiondeblur: Reduces motion blur (strong blur is attenuated, not removed).
vedit.note_detailer: Adds detail and texture. LTX-2 (19B) LoRA used on LTX 2.3: experimental.
vedit.note_outpaint: Extends the frame: the original stays in place, the rest (black) is generated. Describe the whole scene in the prompt. Above ~60% new area the model invents a lot.
vedit.note_restyle: Pick a style image and describe the style (“Make it … style.”). Works well with simple styles; complex textures are weak (v0.1).
vedit.note_cameraman: The camera motion is copied from the reference video. If the result mimics the reference too closely, lower the image strength or change the seed.
vedit.note_lipdub: Dubbing from text (JUST-DUB-IT, Lightricks): the video with its own voice is the reference; write the NEW line (even in another language) and the model generates a voice — with the person's timbre — and new lips, for the same duration as the video. Single speaker only; write in the alphabet of the spoken language (it does not translate: use «Extract and translate»). Keep the line about as long as the original: too long = skipped words, too short = slow voice. To use YOUR OWN audio (song, TTS, file) use the Talk/Sing buttons below, or the experimental «Dubbing from audio» variant.
vedit.note_hdr: Converts an SDR video (Rec.709) to HDR with Lightricks' HDR IC-LoRA: no prompt, the text is a pre-computed file. The player opens a tone-mapped SDR preview; the real HDR video (HEVC 10-bit PQ, BT.2020) and/or the linear EXR sequence sit next to it, with the same name. Feed it an SDR source, not an HDR one. With the dev checkpoint the official distilled LoRA is added.
vedit.restore.prompt_default: Sharp, clean, high-quality footage, natural colors.
vedit.style.image_ph: image that defines the style (becomes frame 0 of the guide)
vedit.cam.ref_ph: video with the camera motion to copy
vedit.cam.img_ph: optional: starting image (i2v); empty = prompt only
vedit.cam.strong_ref_tip: Lower = more motion from the reference (0.5-0.7 recommended). If the result copies the reference, lower it.
vedit.cam.too_small: ⚠ Resolution below 960×512: the reference is followed less well.
vedit.out.dark.tt: Brightens only the source before the outpaint and darkens the result afterwards, so dark areas are not confused with the black bars to generate. Suggested automatically if the video is dark.
vedit.out.dark_auto: [outpaint] dark source: enabled “Dark source (gamma 2.0 / 0.5)”. You can turn it off.
vedit.out.paste_lbl: Paste the original back in the center

vedit.hdr.format_tt: HDR10 video: HEVC 10-bit, PQ, BT.2020 (HDR TVs and phones, Resolve, YouTube). EXR: one linear float file per frame, for compositing (DJV, Nuke, Blender): it is big. The SDR preview is always produced.
vedit.hdr.exposure_tt: Exposure of the SDR PREVIEW in stops (+1 = twice as bright). It does not change the HDR video or the EXRs.
vedit.hdr.hq_tt: Generates twice the frames and keeps every other one: fewer temporal artifacts, double the time.
vedit.hdr.info_out: The player shows the SDR preview; the real HDR file (_HDR_PQ.mp4) and/or the _EXR folder are next to it, with the same name.
vedit.hdr.info_src10: The source is {p}: the HDR LoRA expects 8-bit Rec.709 SDR; an already HDR video (PQ/HLG) must not be used as input.
vedit.note_motion_track: Draw the motion tracks on the image: each track is a subject (or a point of the background) and the ORDER of the points is time. The image is the first frame; describe in the prompt who it is and what they do. With the dev checkpoint the official distilled LoRA is added. The video lasts as long as you choose (official 24 fps, 121 frames = 5 s); the model generates the audio.
vedit.mt.img_ph: starting image: it is the first frame and the background you draw the tracks on
vedit.mt.img_strength_tt: How faithful the first frame stays to the image (1.0 = as in the official recipe).
vedit.mt.no_canvas: No image in the Frame 1 canvas: choose a file.
vedit.mt.handoff_ok: [Motion from tracks] starting image taken from the canvas: draw the tracks and generate.
vedit.mt.handoff_none: [Motion from tracks] no image in the Frame 1 canvas: choose a starting image.
vedit.err_no_tracks: Motion-track: draw at least one track on the image.
vedit.track.tip: Click the image: adds a point to the current track. Drag a point to move it. Right click or «Undo»: removes the last point. THE ORDER OF THE POINTS IS TIME: the first point is where the subject is at the start, the last where it ends up; a track with a single point stays still (useful to hold a background). Keyboard: arrows = move the selected point (Shift = 10 px), Tab = next point, Del = delete the point, N = new track, Ctrl+Z = undo, Enter = add a point at the centre.
vedit.track.new_tt: Closes the current track: the next clicks start another one (one subject per track).
vedit.track.undo_tt: Removes the last added point (also: right click on the image, Ctrl+Z).
vedit.track.preview_tt: Animates the trail of the tracks the way the model will see it.
vedit.track.load_tt: Loads a tracks JSON (also the one from a Lightricks ComfyUI workflow).
vedit.track.save_tt: Saves the tracks as JSON (LTXVSparseTrackEditor node format).
vedit.track.no_image: Choose a starting image to draw the tracks.
vedit.track.empty: Click the image to place the first point of the track.
vid.motion_tracks.tt: Opens AI Video Edit in «Motion from tracks» mode with the starting image already set: you draw where subject and background move and the video follows the tracks.
vedit.mt.audio: Also generate the audio (speech/sounds from the prompt)
vedit.mt.audio_tt: As in the official workflow the model generates the audio together with the video: voice and sounds come from the prompt. Turn it off if the prompt has no speech (otherwise the audio may be noise).
vedit.track.tip_shift: Shift+click: adds a point even on top of another point (to close a loop).
vedit.out.fill.tt: With two opposite bars (top+bottom or left+right) the model mistakes them for letterboxing and leaves them black. With this option, in that case, the original video is shrunk around the centre until the new area is at least 60%: the bars get filled, but the pasted original ends up smaller (less resolution). Turn it off to keep the original at its own scale (bars may stay black).
vedit.out.fill_scaled: original reduced to {p}% so the bars get filled
def.engine.h3up.tt: Upscales the video with MiniMax H3: latent upscaler + one tiled re-draw guided by the h3upscale LoRA (the half-resolution clip is the guide). Needs the H3 Ref2VA model.
def.h3up.model.tt: H3 Ref2VA checkpoint that re-draws the video (the guide LoRA is trained on it). Those not downloaded show ⬇: download them from the «Model weights» tab.
def.h3up.te.tt: Reads the LoRA caption only once: the embedding stays cached, so from the next run the text encoder is not loaded.
def.h3up.mp.tt: Output size as area, EXACT aspect ratio of the source (1 MP = 1024×1024): if the sides are not multiples of 32 a border is added and cropped away at the end, never stretched. It must be larger than the source: this function only enlarges.
def.h3up.guide.tt: The re-draw looks at the half-resolution clip and restores its detail instead of inventing it. Without it, the re-draw starts only from the enlarged latent.
def.h3up.denoise.tt: How hard the single re-draw step works. 0.1 is the original node's value (guided); 0 = enlarge only, without loading the text encoder or the H3 model.
def.h3up.tiles.tt: Largest sequence of one forward. Automatic = computed from the free VRAM after the model is loaded (cap 70,000, the recipe's value). Lower = smaller, more numerous tiles: less VRAM, slower, same seamless merge.
def.h3up.note: Latent upscaler + one tiled re-draw with MiniMax H3, native. Long videos are processed in segments cross-faded in latent space, with tiles merged without seams. The soundtrack stays the original one. MiniMax H3 Community license: excluded territories EU, United Kingdom, USA, South Korea.

f1.kontext.guidance.tt: Kontext guidance (default 2.5, from 1.0 to 4.0): how closely the edit follows the prompt. Lower values soften excessive contrast and saturation; higher values follow the prompt more strongly.

f1.gen.cn.end.tt: Up to which point of the generation the control acts (1.0 = to the end): lower leaves more freedom to the details.
f1.gen.cn.preview.tt: Shows the map (edges/depth/pose) the model will receive, without generating.
f1.gen.cn.no_photo: Choose a guide photo or load a photo into the canvas.

f1.inpaint.cn.scale.tt: ControlNet strength: 0.6-1.0 (recommended by the author); high = follows the masked area more.

f1.mq.mode.tt: Local: redoes the drawn area according to the prompt. Remove: takes the object out and rebuilds the background. Edges: the photo follows the original outlines plus the strokes you draw. Colour: recolours the area with the chosen colour.

f1.mq.erase.tt: Guided edges: normally the strokes you draw ADD to the photo's outlines; with this box they erase the outlines they cross.

canvas.clear_image.tt: Clear the canvas: no start image (the video becomes text-to-video)
canvas.draw_target_tt: Which Integrate mask the brush and eraser draw: Position (red) = where the subject is; Context (yellow) = how much the model may redraw around it.
canvas.ovl_transp_tt: Transparency of this overlay: 0 = solid, 100 = invisible. Display only, it does not change the masks that are sent.
canvas.ovl_show_tt: Shows or hides the position (red) and context (yellow) overlays.
f1.ctx.mode.tt: Context zone: the area around the subject that the model may redraw (hand, shadows, contact). Automatic = the silhouette grown by N pixels; Manual = you draw it.
f1.ctx.pct.tt: Margin around the silhouette, in pixels (the silhouette shape grown all around). 0 = silhouette only; 87 = about the previous zone. No cap: the slider goes to half the long side of the image, the field accepts more; the limit is the image edge.
f1.ctx.from_auto.tt: Fills the context zone with the current automatic one (at the chosen pixel margin).
f1.ctx.clear.tt: Erases the whole drawn context zone: only the subject outline is left.
f1.ctx.unsupported: This engine does not use the context mask: it works from references, without a mask.
f1.ctx.pct_equiv.tt: Equivalent percentage of the silhouette width (read only).
